{{short description|American mathematician (1920-2005)}}
{{Infobox scientist|birth_date=1920|death_date=2005|field=mathematics|education ={{hlist|[[University of Pennsylvania]]|[[Stanford University]]}}|awards=[[Guggenheim Fellow]]}}

'''Paul Charles Rosenbloom''' (1920 in [[Portsmouth, Virginia]] – 2005)<ref>biographical information in [[Gerald L. Alexanderson|Gerald Alexanderson]] ''The Random Walks of George Pólya'', Cambridge University Press 2000</ref> was an American mathematician.

== Life ==
Rosenbloom studied at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where as an undergraduate he became  a [[Putnam Fellow]] in 1941.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 10, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1944 he earned his PhD from [[Stanford University]] under [[Gábor Szegő]] with thesis ''On sequences of polynomials, especially sections of [[power series]]''.<ref>[http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=8371 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> He was a professor of mathematics at [[Brown University]], [[Syracuse University]] (around 1951), the [[University of Minnesota]] (middle to end of the 1950s), and [[Teachers College, Columbia University]] (from the 1960s to his retirement as professor emeritus). His doctoral students include [[Henry Gordon Rice]].

Rosenbloom's research includes analysis, special functions, differential equations, logic, and the teaching of mathematics. In the academic year 1959–1960 he was the director of the Minnesota School Mathematics Center.<ref>[http://conservancy.umn.edu/bitstream/43434/1/1958-59-15.pdf University of Minnesota, Minutes, 1959, pdf] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331001259/http://conservancy.umn.edu/bitstream/43434/1/1958-59-15.pdf |date=2014-03-31 }}</ref>

In 1946 he was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Paul C. Rosenbloom|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/paul-c-rosenbloom/}}</ref> He was at the Institute for Advanced Study for the academic years 1953–1954 and 1971–1972.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paul C. Rosenbloom|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/paul-c-rosenbloom}}</ref>
